'''Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics''' ('''SIAM''') is a professional society dedicated to [[applied mathematics]], computational science, and data science through research, publications, and community. SIAM is the world's largest [[scientific society]] devoted to applied mathematics, and roughly two-thirds of its membership resides within the [[United States]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=MvI8CgAAQBAJ|title=The Princeton Companion to Applied Mathematics|last=Higham|first=Nicholas J.|date=2015-09-15|publisher=[[Princeton University Press]]|isbn=9781400874477|language=en}}</ref> Founded in 1951,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Grier|first=David Alan|date=2006|title=Irene Stegun, the "Handbook of Mathematical Functions", and the Lingering Influence of the New Deal|jstor=27642002|journal=[[The American Mathematical Monthly]]|volume=113|issue=7|pages=585–597|doi=10.2307/27642002}}</ref> the organization began holding annual national meetings in 1954,<ref name=":0">{{cite web|url=http://www-groups.dcs.st-and.ac.uk/~history/Societies/SIAM.html|title=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|date=2005|website=[[MacTutor History of Mathematics archive]]|access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|date=1954|title=News|jstor=2681543|journal=[[The American Statistician]]|volume=8|issue=5|pages=2–22|doi=10.1080/00031305.1954.10482760}}</ref> and now hosts conferences, publishes books and [[scholarly journals]], and engages in advocacy in issues of interest to its membership.<ref name="pp171210" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1991/07/10/us/14-scientific-groups-warn-senate-about-money-drain-of-space-lab.html|title=14 Scientific Groups Warn Senate About Money Drain of Space Lab|last=Leary|first=Warren E.|date=1991-07-10|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=2017-12-10|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}<br />{{Cite news|url=https://www.usnews.com/news/articles/2016-06-28/scientists-warn-congress-not-to-ignore-climate-change|title=Scientists Warn Congress Not to Ignore Climate Change|last=Risen|first=Tom|date=2016-06-28|work=[[U.S. News & World Report]]|access-date=2017-12-10}}<br />{{Cite news|url=http://www.ibtimes.co.uk/american-science-societies-slam-trumps-immigration-ban-muslim-scientists-blocked-us-1604229|title=US scientists protest Trump's 'travel ban' in open letter signed by 150 universities and societies|last=Henriques|first=Martha|date=2017-02-01|work=[[International Business Times UK]]|access-date=2017-12-10|language=en}}<br />{{Cite news|url=https://www.computerworld.com/article/2843572/computer-scientists-say-meme-research-doesnt-threaten-free-speech.html|title=Computer scientists say meme research doesn't threaten free speech|last=Thibodeau|first=Patrick|work=[[Computerworld]]|access-date=2017-12-10|language=en}}</ref> Members include [[engineers]], [[scientists]], and mathematicians, both those employed in academia and those working in industry. The society supports educational institutions promoting [[applied mathematics]].

SIAM is one of the four member organizations of the [[Joint Policy Board for Mathematics]].<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JY3OxdP0h5cC|title=A history of the second fifty years, American Mathematical Society 1939-88|last=Pitcher|first=Everett|date=1988-12-31|publisher=[[American Mathematical Society]]|isbn=9780821896761|language=en}}</ref>

==Membership==
{{main cat|Fellows of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics}}
Membership is open to both individuals and organizations. By the end of its first full year of operation, SIAM had 130 members; by 1968, it had 3,700.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=pS8rAAAAYAAJ|title=Scientific and Technical Societies of the United States|date=1968|publisher=[[National Academy of Sciences]]|language=en}}</ref>

Student members can join SIAM chapters affiliated and run by students and faculty at universities. Most universities with SIAM chapters are in the United States (including [[Harvard University|Harvard]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://harvardsiam.wordpress.com/|title=Harvard University Chapter of SIAM|website=Harvard University Chapter of SIAM|language=en-US|access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref> and [[MIT]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://web.mit.edu/siam/www/|title=MIT SIAM|website=web.mit.edu|access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref>), but SIAM chapters also exist in other countries, for example at [[University of Oxford|Oxford]],<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.science.org/content/article/expand-your-professional-skills-training|title=Expand Your Professional-Skills Training|last=Pain|first=Elisabeth|date=2010-10-01|work=[[Science (journal)|Science]]|access-date=2017-12-10|language=en}}</ref> at the [[École Polytechnique Fédérale de Lausanne]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://siam.epfl.ch/|title=The EPFL Chapter of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|website=The EPFL Chapter of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|language=en-US|access-date=2026-08-25}}</ref> and at [[Peking University]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/students/chapters/|title=Student Chapters|website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref> SIAM publishes the ''SIAM Undergraduate Research Online'', a venue for undergraduate research in applied and computational mathematics. (SIAM also offers the SIAM Visiting Lecturer Program<ref>{{Cite web |title=Visiting Lecturer Program {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/programs/visiting-lecturer-program/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>, which helps arrange visits from industrial mathematicians to speak to student groups about applied mathematics and their own professional experiences.<ref>{{cite book|chapter-url=https://www.springer.com/us/book/9783319022697|title=Educational Interfaces between Mathematics and Industry|author1=S.P Keeler|author2=T.A. Grandine|date=2013|publisher=Springer|editor1-last=Damlamian|editor1-first=Alain|page=31|language=en|chapter=Getting Math off the Ground: Applied Math at Boeing|editor2-last=Francisco|editor2-first=José Rodrigues|editor3-last=Sträßer|editor3-first=Rudolf}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.pme-math.org/conferences/regionalconferences.html|title=Regional Conferences|website=Pi Mu Epsilon|access-date=30 August 2017}}</ref>)

In 2009, SIAM instituted a Fellows program to recognize certain members who have made outstanding contributions to the fields that SIAM serves.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/fellows-program/|title=Fellows Program|publisher=SIAM|access-date=2026-03-16}}</ref>

== Activity groups ==
The society includes a number of activity groups (SIAGs) to allow for more focused group discussions and collaborations. Activity groups organize domain-specific conferences and minisymposia, and award prizes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Activity Groups|url=https://www.siam.org/activity/|website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|access-date=25 April 2017}}</ref>

Unlike special interest groups in similar [[academic associations]] like [[Association for Computing Machinery|ACM]], activity groups are chartered for a fixed period of time, typically for two years, and require submitting a petition to the SIAM Council and Board for renewal. Charter approval is largely based on group size, as topics that were considered hot at one time may have fewer active researchers later.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Crowley|first1=James|last2=Cook|first2=Pam|title=A Closer Look at SIAM Activity Groups|url=http://sinews.briosolutions.com/About-the-Author/ArtMID/7250/ArticleID/836/A-Closer-Look-at-SIAM-Activity-Groups.aspx|website=SIAM News|access-date=25 April 2017}}</ref>

== Publications ==

===Journals===
{{main cat|SIAM academic journals}}
SIAM publishes 19 research journals:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/Publications/journals/ |title=Journals |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2018-07-08}}</ref>
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Applied Mathematics]]'' (SIAP), since 1966
** formerly ''Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics'', since 1953
* ''[[Theory of Probability and Its Applications]]'' (TVP), since 1956
** translation of ''Teoriya Veroyatnostei i ee Primeneniya''
* ''SIAM Review'' (SIREV), since 1959
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization]]'' (SICON), since 1976
** formerly ''SIAM Journal on Control'', since 1966
** formerly ''Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Series A: Control'', since 1962
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Numerical Analysis]]'' (SINUM), since 1966
** formerly ''Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Series B: Numerical Analysis'', since 1964
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Mathematical Analysis]]'' (SIMA), since 1970
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Computing]]'' (SICOMP), since 1972
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications]]'' (SIMAX), since 1988
** formerly ''SIAM Journal on Algebraic and Discrete Methods'', since 1980
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Scientific Computing]]'' (SISC), since 1993
** formerly ''SIAM Journal on Scientific and Statistical Computing'', since 1980
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Discrete Mathematics]]'' (SIDMA), since 1988
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Optimization]]'' (SIOPT), since 1991
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems]]'' (SIADS), since 2002
* ''[[Multiscale Modeling and Simulation]]'' (MMS), since 2003
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Imaging Sciences]]'' (SIIMS), since 2008
* ''[[SIAM Journal on Financial Mathematics]]'' (SIFIN), since 2010
* ''[[SIAM/ASA Journal on Uncertainty Quantification]]'' (JUQ), since 2013
* ''SIAM Journal on Applied Algebra and Geometry'' (SIAGA), since 2017
* ''SIAM Journal on Mathematics of Data Science'' (SIMODS), since 2018
* ''SIAM Journal on Life Sciences'' (SIALS), since 2026

===Books===
SIAM publishes roughly 20 books each year,<ref name=":1">{{Cite journal|last=Armstrong|first=Michelle|date=2013-01-01|title=SIAM eBooks|journal=The Charleston Advisor|volume=14|issue=3|pages=47–49|doi=10.5260/chara.14.3.47}}</ref> including textbooks, conference proceedings and [[monograph]]s. Many of these are issued in themed series, such as "Advances in design and control", "Financial mathematics" and "Monographs on discrete mathematics and applications". In particular, SIAM distributes books produced by [[Gilbert Strang]]'s Wellesley-Cambridge Press, such as his ''Introduction to Linear Algebra'' (5th edition, 2016). Organizations such as libraries can obtain [[Digital rights management|DRM]]-free access to SIAM books in [[eBook]] format for a subscription fee.<ref name=":1" />

===Conferences===
SIAM organizes conferences and meetings throughout the year focused on various topics in applied math and computational science. For example, SIAM has hosted an annual conference on [[data mining]] since 2001.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RyyJkmmp79MC|title=Data Mining Applications for Empowering Knowledge Societies|last=Hakikur|first=Rahman|date=2008-07-31|publisher=IGI Global|isbn=9781599046594|pages=xii|language=en}}</ref> The establishment of the SIAM Conferences on Discrete Mathematics, held every two years, has been regarded as a sign of the growth of [[graph theory]] as a prominent topic of study.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=zA_CAgAAQBAJ|title=A First Course in Graph Theory|last1=Chartrand|first1=Gary|last2=Zhang|first2=Ping|author2-link=Ping Zhang (graph theorist)|date=2013-05-20|publisher=Courier Corporation|isbn=9780486297309|pages=381|language=en}}</ref> The [[International Meshing Roundtable]] is an annual conference that was independently established in 1992 and joined SIAM as a workshop in 2022.

In conjunction with the [[Association for Computing Machinery]], SIAM also organizes the annual [[Symposium on Discrete Algorithms]], using the format of a theoretical computer science conference rather than the mathematics conference format that SIAM typically uses for its conferences.<ref>{{citation|first=Peter|last=Winkler|author-link=Peter Winkler|title=How (and Why!) to Write a SODA Paper|url=http://www.siam.org/meetings/da98/winkler.ps}}. Distributed by Howard Karloff with the [http://www.siam.org/meetings/da98/da98cfp.htm call for papers for SODA 1998].</ref>

SIAM hosts approximately 20 conferences in applied and computational mathematics each year including the SIAM Annual Meeting.<ref>{{Cite web |title=SIAM Mission & History {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/about-us/mission-history/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Prizes and recognition==
SIAM recognizes applied mathematician and computational scientists for their contributions to the fields. Some prizes include:<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/ |title=Prizes, Awards, Lectures and Fellows |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* Germund Dahlquist Prize: Awarded to a young scientist (normally under 45) for original contributions to fields associated with [[Germund Dahlquist]] (numerical solution of differential equations and numerical methods for scientific computing).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/dahlquist.php |title=Germund Dahlquist Prize |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* [[Ralph E. Kleinman Prize]]: Awarded for "outstanding research, or other contributions, that bridge the gap between mathematics and applications...Each prize may be given either for a single notable achievement or for a collection of such achievements."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/major-prizes-lectures/ralph-e-kleinman-prize/ |title=Ralph E. Kleinman Prize |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2025-04-10}}</ref>
* [[J.D. Crawford Prize]]: Awarded to "one individual for recent outstanding work on a topic in nonlinear science, as evidenced by a publication in English in a peer-reviewed journal within the four calendar years preceding the meeting at which the prize is awarded."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/crawford.php |title=J.D. Crawford Prize (SIAG/Dynamical Systems) |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* Jürgen Moser Lecture: Awarded to "a person who has made distinguished contributions to nonlinear science."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/moser.php |title=Jurgen Moser Lecture (SIAG/Dynamical Systems) |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2013-09-28}}</ref>
* [[Richard C. DiPrima Prize]]: Awarded to "a young scientist who has done outstanding research in applied mathematics (defined as those topics covered by SIAM journals) and who has completed his/her doctoral dissertation and completed all other requirements for his/her doctorate during the period running from three years prior to the award date to one year prior to the award date."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/diprima.php |title=The Richard C. DiPrima Prize |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* [[George Pólya Prize]]: "is given every two years, alternately in two categories: (1) for a notable application of combinatorial theory; (2) for a notable contribution in another area of interest to George Pólya such as approximation theory, complex analysis, number theory, orthogonal polynomials, probability theory, or mathematical discovery and learning."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/polya.php |title=George Pólya Prize |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* [[W. T. and Idalia Reid Prize]]: Awarded for research in and contributions to areas of [[differential equation]]s and control theory.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/reid.php |title=W. T. and Idalia Reid Prize in Mathematics |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* [[Theodore von Kármán Prize]]: Awarded for "notable application of mathematics to mechanics and/or the engineering sciences made during the five to ten years preceding the award."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/vonkarman.php |title=Theodore von Kármán Prize |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* [[James H. Wilkinson]] Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing: Awarded for "research in, or other contributions to, [[numerical analysis]] and scientific computing during the six years preceding the award."<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/wilkinson.php |title=James H. Wilkinson Prize in Numerical Analysis and Scientific Computing |publisher=SIAM |access-date=2012-12-04}}</ref>
* I. E. Block Community Lecture: Awarded to a member of the scientific community known for "engaging nontechnical as well as technical audiences in the role that applied mathematics plays in solving topical, real world problems."<ref>{{Cite web |title=I. E. Block Community Lecture {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/major-prizes-lectures/i-e-block-community-lecture/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>
* SIAM Industry Prize: Awarded to an individual or team for "outstanding contributions to the effective application of mathematical sciences to industry."<ref>{{Cite web |date=2026-10-15 |title=SIAM Industry Prize {{!}} SIAM |url=https://www.siam.org/programs-initiatives/prizes-awards/major-prizes-lectures/siam-industry-prize/ |access-date=2026-08-27 |website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics |language=en-US}}</ref>

===John von Neumann Lecture===
The [[John von Neumann Lecture]] prize was established in 1959 with funds from [[IBM]] and other industry corporations, and is awarded for "outstanding and distinguished contributions to the field of applied mathematical sciences and for the effective communication of these ideas to the community".<ref>{{cite web|title=The John von Neumann Lecture|url=https://www.siam.org/prizes/sponsored/vonneumann.php|website=Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|access-date=25 April 2017}}</ref> The recipient receives a monetary award and presents a survey lecture at the Annual Meeting.

===MathWorks Math Modeling (M3) Challenge===
The [[MathWorks Math Modeling Challenge]] is an applied mathematics modeling competition for high school students in the United States. Scholarship prizes totaled $60,000 in 2006, and have since been raised to $100,000.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9804E5D6153FF930A15757C0A9609C8B63|title=That Was Easy: Social Security Problem Solved|last=Gordon|first=Jane|date=2006-04-23|work=[[The New York Times]]|access-date=2017-12-10|language=en-US|issn=0362-4331}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagner |first=Ryan |date=2026-04-29 |title=Edison Students Land Top Spot in Prestigious International Math Competition |url=https://m3challenge.siam.org/newsroom/edison-students-land-top-spot-in-prestigious-international-math-competition/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=M3 Challenge |language=en-US}}</ref> It is funded by Mathworks.<ref name="pt171209">{{cite news|last1=Persinger|first1=Ryanne|title=U.S. Education Department looks into discrimination claims|url=http://www.phillytrib.com/u-s-education-department-looks-into-discrimination-claims/article_fbdd0809-3db5-5e22-b09b-ae31cdafe9a7.html|access-date=10 December 2017|newspaper=[[Philadelphia Tribune]]|date=December 9, 2017}}</ref><ref name="fo170717">{{cite magazine|last1=Knapp|first1=Alex|title=Moody's Foundation Pulls Sponsorship Of High School Math Competition|url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/alexknapp/2017/07/17/moodys-foundation-pulls-sponsorship-of-high-school-math-competition/#14d7849248d0|access-date=10 December 2017|magazine=[[Forbes]]|date=July 17, 2017}}</ref> Originally, the prize was sponsored by the financial services company [[Moody's Corporation|Moody's]] and known as the ''Moody's Mega Math Challenge.''<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.economist.com/business/2008/02/26/companies-with-a-heart|title=Companies with a heart: In search of better corporate philanthropy|date=2008-02-26|access-date=2017-12-10|newspaper=[[The Economist]]}}</ref>

==Leadership==
The chief elected officer of SIAM is the president, elected for a single two-year term.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.siam.org/about/pdf/bylaws.pdf |title=Microsoft Word - newbylaws2.doc |access-date=2017-12-10}}</ref>  SIAM employs a chief executive officer and staff.<ref name="pp171210"/>
